title: UDLM state record — one record per lifecycle state
description: Ruling 071 (four-states.md §2.7). An entity's four states are four records — intent, requested, realized, discovered — each written by exactly one party, each immutable, each carrying one envelope plus one body. The envelope: entity_uuid (the identity every edge points at; never changes), record_uuid (this record, time-ordered), state, generation, supersedes, the tenant, the class pin, when and by which clock. The bodies: intent carries the fields as written and actor provenance; requested carries the fields after assembly and policy, the layers applied and left unapplied, the policies evaluated with their decisions, the fulfillment status when the request is refused or blocked, and the intent it came from; realized carries the fields as built, the outputs other things bind to, which provider instance built it, health, placement, the natural keys discovery recognizes it by, and the requested record it realizes; discovered carries what a sweep saw and how it was matched. One closed schema for the four kinds, dispatched on record_type; per-state rules say which body fields belong. The merged 'entity as it flows through the four states' shape (entity-view.schema.json) is a READ MODEL assembled from these records, never written; its blocks are $refs into this schema's $defs, so the stored form owns every shape and the view can never disagree with it.

record_type.description: Dispatch key; MUST agree with `state` (intent_record ⇔ Intent, …).

state.description: Which of the four states this record is. One record, one state, one author. Capitalized as the four-state vocabulary is; `record_type` is its lowercase dispatch key.

entity_uuid.description: The thing this record is about. Stable for the entity's life (RFC 9562 v4, minted at intent); the universal linking key (four-states.md §3); what every dependency edge targets.

record_uuid.description: This record (RFC 9562 v7 — time-ordered, so a state's stream sorts by identity). A new version of a state is a NEW record_uuid naming its predecessor in `supersedes`; records are never edited (ADR-051).

generation.description: The request cycle this record belongs to. Increments on each new intent; a realized record carries the generation it realized (the observedGeneration reading).

supersedes.description: The record_uuid(s) this record replaces within the same state's stream. Absent or empty on the first record of a state — the supersession chain four-states.md §2.3 asks for.

tenant_uuid.description: REQUIRED owning Tenant, as on entity-view.schema.json.

resource_type.description: The class the entity is an instance of — the canonical name, never a short_name (CLS-007).

type_version.description: The class version this record was authored or realized against (ADR-051 pin, human half).

type_digest.description: OPTIONAL exact half of the pin (type@sha256:<hex>).

type_ref.description: The `$id` of the pinned class or served spec.

handle.description: ADVISORY human-readable identity of the ENTITY (identifier-scheme §3), in the wire grammar (WIR-003); the uuid is authoritative.

at.description: When this record was written, RFC 3339 normalized to UTC 'Z' (WIR-007); the clock is named by time_source.

origin.description: How this record came to exist: declared by its author; derived from a discovery (brownfield adoption); backfilled after the fact.

fields.description: The entity's fields, typed by its class (the flat spec compiled from it). Values are not re-validated here.

outputs.description: The typed outputs the class declares — its binding surface (data-model-core [D8.3]). Realized and discovered only.

intent_ref.description: Requested only: the record_uuid of the intent record this was assembled from.

requested_ref.description: Realized only: the record_uuid of the requested record this realizes — every realized record is traceable to exactly one (four-states.md §2.3).

provider.description: Realized only: the provider INSTANCE that built it — a resolvable reference (handle or uuid), not free text. The merged schema carried only a string here, and nothing recorded which offering actually answered.

matched_by.description: Discovered only: which correlation-id schemes matched this observation to `entity_uuid` (dcm ADR-017 Decision C). Empty on an unclaimed observation.

portability.portability_notes: Realized entirely from Type-scope elements; strip outputs, provider and correlation ids and `fields` is a valid new intent.

provenance.description:
FIELD-LEVEL PROVENANCE (#191 / E4): keyed by dot-path into the spec, an ordered history of who set each field. UDLM carries this record; the control plane writes it during assembly (a Layer, a Policy, an actor) and at realization (a Provider). It is the same record the audit chain consumes (G3) — never a parallel model. Each array is the ordered modification chain for that field: entries map 1:1 to the audit-provenance modifications[] records (origin = the first entry), with optional `sequence` for explicit ordering and `operation_type` for the write semantics.

A HISTORY CLAIM ON A WORKING RECORD IS NOT CITABLE AS LINEAGE. Only sealed, chained and anchored records carry that weight (ADR-059) — this block is readable, but a consumer needing provable lineage reads the seal's `udlm_provenance` facet (`registry/facets/udlm-provenance.facet.json`), not this. `integrity` is what makes the record's own timeline verifiable on its own; this is the convenience copy of who set what.

kind.description: Canonical provenance source kinds (data-model-core §6/§7): layer = layer assembly wrote the value; policy = a policy set/enriched/locked it; actor = an authenticated identity wrote it directly ('consumer' in older documents maps here — a consumer acts as an actor); provider = the realizing provider reported it; discovery = a discovery cycle observed it; rehydration = a rehydration pipeline restored it; override = an authorized override set it (DCM ADR-013).

actor.description: The authenticated identity on whose behalf the change was made.

operation_type.description: Write semantics of this provenance entry (the audit-provenance modifications[] operation, normalized): set = value written/replaced; merge = value combined with the prior value (e.g. list/object merge during layer assembly); remove = value deleted. Optional — omitted entries are read as `set`.

sequence.description: Explicit position of this entry in the field's ordered modification chain (audit-provenance modifications[].sequence). Optional — when omitted, array order is the chain order.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps). The producing clock is attributed via the nearest time_source.

previous_value.description: Value before this change (any JSON type), for the audit diff.

dependencies.description: Resolved instance-level edges (the realized form of the type's relationships). A binding records the value pulled from the target's realized output — data movement, not transformation (T4).

bound_field.description: The field on this entity the bound value populated (binds_to data movement, T4). Never a relation label — relation semantics live in `relation`.

resolved_at.description: RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps). The producing clock is attributed via the nearest time_source.

target_handle.description: ADVISORY handle of the target at reference time (identifier-scheme §3). target_uuid is authoritative; a handle mismatch on resolution is drift (REF-002), not failure.

strength.description: depends_on only. hard = target unavailability blocks this entity; soft = degrade-don't-break (docs/spec/foundations/service-dependencies.md DEP-006) — informs ordering but never blocks.

relation.description: The declared relation name from the pinned type's relationship vocabulary (relationships[].name) — REL-001: must be declared; REL-003: refines, never overrides, kind's ordering semantics, so graph consumers that read only kind+strength stay correct. NOT bound_field (which is strictly the data-binding field of a binds_to edge).

status.description: Realized-state health (OSAC-/K8s-style). Reported by the provider; not part of the four-state axis.

type.description: The condition being reported. Open by design (K8s convention) — health, recovery and provider-specific conditions all live here. ONE FAMILY IS CLOSED: the fulfillment conditions `blocked-transient` | `blocked-permanent` | `refused` | `dependency-cancelled` (service-dependencies DEP-017), which say why a member has not reached Realized yet. That family is closed because its members carry PROPAGATION semantics — a dependent inherits transitively, and transient waits where permanent refuses — so a fifth spelling is not a new condition, it is a member of this family nobody can act on.

blocked_on.description: WHAT this member is waiting on — a reference to the blocking record. REQUIRED on a fulfillment condition (DEP-017): 'blocked' without a blocker is not actionable, and the root-naming obligation is the whole point of the family — a blocked-permanent app three hops from the refused volume is only useful if the volume is reachable from it. On an inherited condition this names the IMMEDIATE blocker, not the root; the root is found by walking, never by copying it down the chain (DRV-001).

last_transition_time.description: RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps). The producing clock is attributed via the nearest time_source.

then.description: A member blocked BY something names what. `refused` is exempt: it is the root of a chain rather than a link in one, so its cause is its own `reason` — there is nothing upstream to point at.

sovereignty.description: The sovereign placement of the realized entity. These are realized from `immutable`/createOnly type fields — they cannot change without replace + Governance-Matrix re-evaluation (cross-cutting P4).

plane_attestations.description: R2 evidence binding — per-plane attestation that this entity's sovereignty is BACKED, not merely declared. Each ties an enforcement plane to the accreditation that satisfies it plus the verification result — the *why-entitled*, not just the verdict (a `zone`/`classification` alone records the claim, not its authorization). Written by the control plane at realization from the resolved accreditation (accreditation-and-authorization-matrix.md §3.7 verify-then-appraise, §3.8 enforcement-plane).

plane.description: Which enforcement plane this attestation covers (provider-contract §2 enforcement_plane).

accreditation_uuid.description: The accreditation artifact that satisfies the plane requirement — the authorizing evidence the claim binds to.

verification_result.description: The two-gate appraisal outcome (accreditation-and-authorization-matrix.md §3.7). An unattested/failed plane cannot satisfy a regulated-zone requirement on the provider's word.

locality.description: R2 evidence binding — the concrete fault-domain / physical locality this entity was placed in (the per-resource anchor the placement grammar keys on — DCM ADR-019 placement, ADR-010 SharedFaultDomain). Written by the provider/the control plane at realization; the basis for anti-affinity, blast-radius, and per-resource jurisdiction checks.

topology_ref.description: Reference to the Topology fault-domain / location resource this entity resolved onto.

fault_domain.description: The named fault domain (e.g. rack / host / zone) — the grouping key for SharedFaultDomain (ADR-010).

correlation_ids.description: Stable natural keys independent of any observer, for entity resolution across discovery sources (dcm ADR-017 Decision C): a new observation matching an existing entity by these keys MERGES into that entity's uuid — one real resource, one entity uuid, never a duplicate. Every discovery source MUST emit them.

scheme.description: The kind of natural key. provider-id = the owning provider's own resource identifier (Avenue-1 discovery).

adopted_standards.description: ADOPTED-STANDARD BINDINGS (T5): for each external standard adopted by this entity's type, the realized record of the control plane's version negotiation — the requested range, the provider's chosen version, the negotiated effective version, and whether the control plane translated between versions (ADS-003/004/008). UDLM carries this record; the control plane (Policy) produces it and writes it to the audit log. The external data itself is NOT carried here — it is referenced from its Information Provider via the identity join.

portability.description: INSTANCE portability: the realized entity's actual portability, DEGRADED from the type's declared classification when the entity carries provider-specific data (Provider-Class `SharedDataElement`s — ADR-038; schema realization #199; the retired `provider_extensions` carrier is removed per #202). Base-type-declared, instance-degraded — never silently presented as fully portable. When degraded, the consumer MUST be notified before/at realization (resource-type-hierarchy Transparency principle); a portability-degradation event is emitted.

classification.description: Effective instance classification. Narrows from the type's declared value when provider-specific data is present (e.g. portable -> provider-specific). COMPUTED by the control plane, not provider-declared.

portability_breaking.description: true iff this entity cannot be moved to another provider of the same type without loss — i.e. it carries provider-specific data. COMPUTED: any provider-specific (Provider-Class) element ⇒ true.

portability_notes.description: Human-readable explanation surfaced to the consumer: which provider-specific elements make it non-portable and which provider(s) it is thereby bound to. Where a hard `provider_preference` is in force, say so here and say what it costs: a hard pin makes rehydration PROVIDER-DEPENDENT, which is a different failure from lossy movement — replaying the intent against a provider that no longer exists does not degrade, it fails. Whether it counts as degradation at all is policy's call; what the record owes is the fact and the distinction.

bound_providers.description: Provider handles this entity is bound to via provider-specific data. Moving to a provider not in this set would drop that data.

consumer_notified.description: Transparency record (resource-type-hierarchy Transparency principle): the deviation MUST be surfaced to the consumer before/at realization — silent non-portability is prohibited.

expected_observation.description: The DECLARED observation expectation this entity is judged against (ADR-048 — staleness as declared expectation). Staleness verdicts — current | stale_expected | stale_deviant — are DERIVED by comparing observation age (states.discovered.at / drift.checked_at) with this declaration; no verdict is ever stored. Where absent, the OBS-005 profile TTL (docs/spec/foundations/service-dependencies.md) applies as the fallback. When the expectation is composed at a coarser scope (e.g. a group-wide offline window resolved per ADR-015), this block carries the RESOLVED value — its provenance rides the standard per-field provenance record, never a hand-typed copy.

cadence.description: ISO 8601 duration — expect an observation at least this often (e.g. P1D, PT4H, P30D).

window.description: A declared expected-contact period: observations are expected only within it, and their absence outside it is normal by declaration. Alternative to cadence; declare either or both.

opens.description: Start of the expected-contact period (RFC 3339 date or instant).

closes.description: End of the expected-contact period (RFC 3339 date or instant).

recurs.description: Whether the window repeats (a seasonal fleet declares annually).

on_exceeded.description: What an overdue observation MEANS: normal -> the derived verdict is stale_expected (a healthy state); finding -> stale_deviant (the alarm). This is the judgment declaration that lets seasonal absence be healthy while true deviance still alarms.

process.description: Process-execution axis (resource-service-entities §6.3; data-model-core §3 [D7]). REQUIRED on entities whose Resource Type has family: Process (the Job class) — validate.py enforces this via the registry. The universal lifecycle_state still applies (a playbook that exists and is adopted is Realized/Discovered); execution_state is a SEPARATE axis tracking each RUN and never changes lifecycle_state.

execution_state.description: The current run's state (§6.2). Distinct from lifecycle_state.

affected_entities.description: Entities this process created/modified/decommissioned/read (§6.3). §6.4: each affected entity's realized provenance MUST cite THIS process's uuid as the change source.

priced_by.description: PROPOSED (cost-metering-linkage.md; ADR-COST-002). Per-INSTANCE cost-model reference override — overrides the resource type's `priced_by` default for this entity (per-customer/contract pricing, whose lifecycle stays external). UDLM never defines the model's contents (ADR-COST-001).

information_provider_uuid.description: The registered serve_data:cost provider (the cost engine).

external_model_id.description: Opaque id of the cost model within that engine.

constituents.description: For a Composite Entity: the constituents and their per-component realized state (docs/spec/foundations/template-composition-model.md).

metadata.description: Human-facing context. Operational commentary lives in `notes` — it is data ABOUT the record, never used for resolution.

notes.description: Auditable operational notes: each entry is attributed and timestamped — never an anonymous mutable blob.

at.description: When recorded. RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps). The producing clock is attributed via the nearest time_source.

author.description: Who/what recorded it (person, agent+session, or process uuid).

integrity.description:
THE RESOURCE CHAIN — the record's own version timeline, made tamper-evident in the record (ADR-059 Decision 2). Every new version appends, whichever pathway caused it, so a Discovered write is as tamper-evident as an Intent one.

WHY IT IS ON THE RECORD AND NOT ONLY IN THE LEDGER. Records are unbounded in lifetime; stores are not. A realized entity may run for a decade while audit is retained for years and observability for weeks, so an operation that reaches into the ledger to verify itself works until the day it silently does not. The chain answers `has this record been altered` without any other system — which is ADR-059's record-content test applied to integrity itself.

ONE-WAY BRIDGE. The ledger's seal embeds the working copy and this head; the record never references the ledger. That direction is deliberate: operations must never hang on compliance storage being reachable.

CLAIMS DISCIPLINE. This is a STATE claim — `the bytes of this version, and what preceded it`. It is not provenance, lineage or history, and presenting it under such a heading is a defect (ADR-059 Decision 1). Only sealed, chained, anchored ledger records make history claims.

head.description: This version's link. Computed over the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form of the record MINUS `integrity` itself, with `previous` folded in — the same strip-and-canonicalize machinery the identity digest uses (ADR-051), so the two can never disagree about what the bytes of a record are. Self-exclusion is not a convention but a necessity: a digest that covered itself would be uncomputable.

previous.description: The prior version's `head`, or null at the first version. Null means `chain root`, and it is distinct from ABSENT: an omitted `previous` on a later version is a broken chain, while an explicit null is a beginning. A verifier that could not tell them apart would read every truncation as a fresh start.

algorithm.description: How `head` was computed: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical form. Stated rather than assumed so a future algorithm is a declared migration and not a silent reinterpretation of existing heads — a verifier reading an old record must know which rule produced it.

hashed_by.description: OPTIONAL — the control-plane identity that computed this head. The control plane is the sole hasher (ADR-059); recorded where an estate runs more than one and needs to attribute a break to an instance.

audit.description: Linkage to the tamper-evident audit log (AUD-001/002). UDLM carries the reference (the Merkle head + leaf count); the control plane produces and proves the chain (G3).

log_head.description: Hash of the latest audit leaf for this entity (RFC 9162 Merkle).

handle.description: ADVISORY human-readable identity (docs/spec/contracts/identifier-scheme.md §3). The uuid is the authoritative identity; the handle aids review and drift detection (a resolved-uuid whose current handle disagrees with a reference's recorded handle is drift, not failure). Never resolve by handle alone.

provider_preference.description:
A named provider this request PREFERS — the pin (ADR-050).

IT DECIDES WHICH ELIGIBLE PROVIDER, NEVER WHETHER AN INELIGIBLE ONE IS REACHED. The `effective_capabilities` ceiling applies at the dispatch boundary on every path (`PRV-009`, `PRV-011`), so a pin naming a provider that has not been admitted for what the request needs is refused with `placement.capability_mismatch` BEFORE dispatch, carrying the required-versus-declared comparison.

The pin is absolute over the CHOICE and not over CAPABILITY. That is what keeps one sentence true everywhere — the ceiling always applies — instead of true-with-an-exception, and an exception is the thing a reader cannot see from the rule.

A DELIBERATE BYPASS IS POLICY'S, NOT THE MODEL'S (ADR-008 peer test). Whether an operator may dispatch outside a declared capability is an operational choice a conformant implementation is entitled to make differently, so UDLM fixes only the invariant such a bypass would be an exception TO. A field here that could waive the ceiling would move that choice into the substrate and make every implementation inherit one estate's risk appetite.

provider.description: The preferred provider, as a URF reference — authored by handle, resolved to the uuid form (WIR-004).

reason.description: Why this provider is preferred. Carried for the human reading a placement decision; never evaluated.

set_by.description: Who pinned it — an administrator, or the policy that did. A preference nobody can be asked about is one nobody can safely remove.

strength.description:
Whether placement may substitute.

`soft` — a preference. If the named provider is ineligible, at capacity or absent, placement chooses another eligible one. The request stays portable.

`hard` — a requirement. Placement does not substitute; if the named provider cannot serve the request it is refused. This is the form operators genuinely need and the one that costs something, so it is stated rather than inferred from context.

REQUIRED, WITH NO DEFAULT (NDF-001). A pin whose strength is unstated would be read as soft by one implementation and hard by another, and the difference is whether a request silently moves provider or silently fails.

NEITHER VALUE BYPASSES THE CEILING. `effective_capabilities` applies at the dispatch boundary on every path — a hard pin naming an ineligible provider is refused before dispatch, exactly as a soft one is (ADR-050). Hard changes whether placement SUBSTITUTES, never what is REACHABLE.

acknowledged.description:
The consumer was told what a hard pin costs, and when.

WHY THIS IS A RECORD AND NOT A WARNING. A warning is shown once, to the person choosing, and is gone. This is read by whoever inherits the request — the person harmed by a hard pin is rarely the one who set it, but the one who tries to move or rehydrate it later and finds the named provider gone.

WHAT UDLM DOES AND DOES NOT DECIDE. The model carries the pin, its strength, and this acknowledgement, and makes all three readable — `provider_preference.*` resolves as a request-payload dot-path, so a policy can match on it. WHETHER a hard pin degrades portability, and what it means for rehydration, is POLICY's call: an estate with one provider loses nothing by pinning to it, and an estate with five loses a great deal. Computing that here would make UDLM decide an estate's exposure for it.

standard.description: External standard name, e.g. FOCUS, OpenCost.

requested_version.description: The version pin/range the consumer or type required.

provider_version.description: The version the bound provider emits/consumes (from its support matrix).

effective_version.description: The version actually used after negotiation (the system-of-record fact).

translated.description: True when the control plane translated between provider_version and effective_version (ADS-004) — a Policy act, lowering confidence for derived values.

translation_ref.description: Reference to the deterministic migration used (preferably the standard's own published migration).

provider_uuid.description: The provider / Information Provider that served the adopted data (lookup-only; not owned here — ADS-007).

resolved_at.description: RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps). The producing clock is attributed via the nearest time_source.

data_role.description: Data ROLE — the purpose axis (ADR-PROV-001; docs/spec/contracts/data-roles.md), ORTHOGONAL to data_classification (sensitivity). Governs dispatch: only `execution` crosses to a provider by default. execution = the provider needs it to realize the resource (the dispatch contract); assembly = control-plane assembly record (unapplied contributions, excluded layers); governance/audit/cost = other control-plane concerns. A provider may opt into non-execution roles via accepts_roles, subject to Governance-Matrix policy.

at.description: RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps). The producing clock is attributed via the nearest time_source.

roles.description: Field/section role OVERRIDES, keyed by a dot-path into `fields` (a leaf = field-level; a prefix = section-level). Default is `execution` (dispatched); list ONLY non-execution exceptions here (succinct usage). Precedence: field-level path > section-level prefix > default execution (docs/spec/contracts/data-roles.md cascade).

assembly.description: Non-dispatched ASSEMBLY record (role: assembly; ADR-PROV-001). Control-plane only — MUST NOT be naturalized into the provider dispatch payload, and MUST NOT be copied into states.realized. Meaningful on the Requested snapshot: the record of what was offered but not applied, and which candidate layers were excluded.

id.description: uuid of the layer/policy/actor/provider that offered it.

attempted_value.description: The value this source offered but that was NOT applied (any type).

unapplied.description: Per-field 'road not taken' — contributions offered but not applied, each with source, attempted_value, disposition, and reason (the winning chain is in `provenance`).

excluded_layers.description: Candidate layers dropped at resolution (LAY-003) and why.

applied.description: The layers and policies that CONTRIBUTED to this requested state, in precedence order — the positive half of the assembly record (`unapplied` and `excluded_layers` are the negative half). What ran, as a list; which field each set is per-field provenance.

id.description: uuid of the layer/policy/actor/provider that offered it.

version.description: The version of the layer or policy that contributed.

fields.description: dot-paths this contribution set or narrowed.

policies.description: Requested only: the policies evaluated for this request cycle and what each decided — the statement of what ran, beside the per-field provenance that says what each changed.

policy.description: The policy record, by handle or uuid.

fields.description: dot-paths the policy set, narrowed or stripped, if any.
